rfm_tuples.interpretation: This is the strongest single Form-4 negative signal possible in the Signal OS framework: a -48.5% drawdown with absolutely zero insider conviction. The entire executive suite (CEO, CFO, COO, CAO, GC) was a net seller for 17 months and not one of them put $1 of personal capital to work even at the post-drawdown bottom. Compare to ABG (forward-test peer) where CEO bought $1.03M at $205 post-10-K. The asymmetry is total. Multiple sells (CEO 5/22/2025, CFO 5/27, dir. Lissy 5/28) clustered in late May 2025 BEFORE the stock collapsed from ~$130 to ~$72 by cutoff — selling-into-strength pattern. Even allowing that BFAM has a long pattern of routine 10b5-1 sales, the COMPLETE absence of any contrarian buy after a 48% decline directly contradicts management's stated confidence.

rfm_tuples.f: Reconcile reported FY2025 financial improvement against the -48.5% drawdown. Mode B: if all reported metrics are strong, what is the market repricing? Search for the source of dissonance in disclosure.

rfm_tuples.M_value: Reported FY2025 numbers are unambiguously strong on every disclosed metric. Same-center occupancy improved YoY (40% >70% enrolled in Q4'25 vs lower in Q4'24). Cash from operations $350.7M (+$13.2M YoY). Cash position grew to $140.1M. Yet stock is down -48.5% to ~$72. Risk-factor disclosure flags "recent incidents in both the U.S. and U.K. involving allegations of mistreatment and abuse of children by former employees" — language NEW or escalated in this 10-K, and which "have currently...lead to increased regulatory review and oversight, and clients seeking to curtail or terminate our services. Such incidents have, and may in the future, result in substantial litigation or the suspension or revocation of child care licenses." Note that incidents are described with present-tense ongoing impact ("have currently...lead") — language softer disclosure would have phrased as hypothetical.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B finding. There is a wide gap between the bright headline and the -48.5% drawdown. Issuer attributes drawdown ambiguity to vague "dynamic operating environment ... challenging macroeconomic conditions" while the risk-factor language reveals an escalated abuse/safeguarding narrative (US AND UK). Combined with the insider tape (BFAM-01/02), the most consistent interpretation is that the disclosed FY2025 numbers do not yet reflect the impact of those incidents on client retention and that insiders correctly anticipated material brand/reputation damage that the GAAP statements have not yet captured.

rfm_tuples.f: Mode B (implied verification): if 'recent incidents' have 'currently' led to 'increased regulatory review and oversight' and 'clients seeking to curtail or terminate' services, those impacts should be quantifiable. Test whether Note 19 (Commitments & Contingencies) or Legal Proceedings discloses any specific accruals, litigation, or client-loss figures.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (Item 3 Legal Proceedings + Note 19 Commitments and Contingencies cross-check)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Legal Proceedings (Item 3) is boilerplate: "We are, from time to time, subject to claims, suits, and matters arising in the ordinary course of business ... legal matters will not have a material adverse effect." Note 19 says "The Company's accruals for outstanding legal matters are not material, individually or in the aggregate." NO specific accruals, NO disclosed settlements, NO quantified client losses, NO disclosed regulatory enforcement actions or license suspensions despite the risk factor stating these are "current" effects. This is a Mode-B gap: the risk-factor language is more specific/severe than the legal/financial disclosures support.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catch. Issuer uses Risk Factors to flag US + UK abuse incidents with current operating impact, but Item 3 and Note 19 disclose nothing material. Either (a) the impacts are material but not yet accrued / not yet litigated to a quantifiable stage (likely given the present-tense risk language) and will land in 2026, OR (b) the risk language is overcautious. Insider tape (BFAM-01) strongly suggests (a). This is precisely the kind of escalating-disclosure-language-before-financial-recognition that the framework is designed to detect.

Bears must be pricing in client losses, regulatory action, or growth deceleration not yet in the numbers.

summary: BFAM is a -48.5% drawdown name where the FORENSIC tape strongly REINFORCES the SHORT thesis. Headline FY2025 financials are unambiguously strong (revenue +9.2% to $2.93B, adj EBITDA +19% to $487M, back-up care +19%, net leverage 1.65x, $329M buyback remaining, clean Deloitte opinion) — yet across 91 Form 4 filings spanning 17 months and the full drawdown, ZERO open-market purchases were made by ANY of 17+ named insiders. The CEO, CFO, COO, GC, CAO, Chair, and 9 directors collectively sold $18.1M and bought $0. A particularly damaging cluster of 4 insider sells (CEO + CFO + Chair + a director) in the single week of May 22-29, 2025 at $125-132 immediately preceded the major decline. Concurrently, the FY2025 10-K (filed 2026-02-26) ESCALATED its risk-factor language around 'recent incidents in both the U.S. and U.K. involving allegations of mistreatment and abuse of children by former employees' with present-tense 'have currently...lead to increased regulatory review and oversight, and clients seeking to curtail or terminate our services' framing — yet Item 3 Legal Proceedings and Note 19 disclose ZERO specific accruals, litigation, or client losses. The Mode-B gap (escalating disclosure language preceding financial recognition) plus the total-zero insider conviction is the Signal OS framework's classic 'honest-disclosure of brewing damage' pattern. The business itself is not levered or distressed; the bear case is reputational/client-attrition still flowing through the P&L. Verdict: SHORT-tier. Severity: 2 PASS / 0 UNVERIFIABLE / 3 MODERATE / 3 SEVERE / 1 RED_FLAG_NEGATIVE.
